A01.alt: European buyers do not decide on your operation. They decide on your evidence.

S01.alt: You received a request from a European buyer. A questionnaire, a clause, a data request. With a deadline.

A02.alt: The law is European. The request lands in a Brazilian inbox.

S02.alt: Seu comprador europeu não vai esperar a lei entrar em vigor para pedir evidência. Ele já está pedindo.

A03.alt: Five levels. One question: can a buyer act on your file without calling you?

S03.alt: This morning's note: most exporter files sit at SEMM level 1 or 2. The buyer needs level 3.

A04.alt: "Our operation is fine." Usually true. Also irrelevant.

S04.alt: Licença no jurídico. Dados de produção numa planilha. Origem no papel da cooperativa. Cláusula assinada e nunca lida contra o arquivo.

S05.alt: The questionnaire was answered "yes". The contract says "supplier shall provide evidence upon request". Nobody checked whether the two match.

A06.alt: Every claim in a supplier file should carry a label: Fact, Interpretation or Hypothesis.

S06.alt: Pergunta para o CFO exportador: do que você respondeu ao último questionário europeu, quanto era fato documentado e quanto era afirmação?

A07.alt: One week of notes. The thread so far:

S07.alt: For European procurement, compliance and sustainability teams:

A08.alt: Since 1 January 2026, CBAM is in its definitive period. Translation for a Brazilian exporter: the embedded-emissions number of your product now has a price attached on the importer's side.

S08.alt: Exporta aço, alumínio, cimento ou fertilizante para a União Europeia? Desde janeiro de 2026 o importador paga certificado CBAM com base nas emissões incorporadas do que ele compra de você.

A09.alt: The default value is not a technical fallback. It is a commercial penalty you pay without seeing the invoice.

A10.alt: What a CBAM data request actually asks a Brazilian producer for. Not the regulation — the e-mail.

S10.alt: Sete blocos num pedido de dados CBAM. A maioria dos exportadores brasileiros responde os dois primeiros e trava no quinto.

A11.alt: CBAM is a cost on the European side. That makes it a procurement lever on the Brazilian side.

S11.alt: Exporter A has installation-level data. Exporter B has a sustainability letter. Same product, different landed cost in Europe.

A12.alt: Who owns the number? In most Brazilian producers we review, the honest answer is "nobody".

S12.alt: Quem é o dono do número de emissões incorporadas na sua empresa?

A13.alt: A note on Scope 1 and 2 reporting versus CBAM embedded emissions. They are related. They are not the same number.

S13.alt: You already have a GHG inventory. Your importer still asked for CBAM data. Those are different numbers — and the gap between them is allocation and documentation, not measurement.

A14.alt: A five-point readiness check for Brazilian exporters of CBAM goods. Score yourself honestly.

S14.alt: Cinco perguntas do checklist CBAM desta manhã. Se você respondeu "não" ou "parcialmente" em duas ou mais, o importador europeu está, com boa probabilidade, declarando o seu produto com valor padrão.

S15.alt: "Prove origin and geolocation for every shipment."

A16.alt: The EUDR obligation belongs to the EU operator. The EUDR evidence belongs to you. That asymmetry defines the next six months.

S16.alt: Café, cacau, soja, carne, couro, madeira, borracha. Se você exporta para a UE, o seu comprador precisa de uma declaração de due diligence a partir de 30 de dezembro de 2026 — e os dados que sustentam essa declaração estão com você.

A17.alt: Geolocation is the data point most Brazilian files have — and almost none have in usable form.

S17.alt: Coordinates on WhatsApp. A CAR polygon for the farm. A supplier list without a map. A buyer who needs plot-level geolocation per export lot.

A18.alt: Deforestation-free is half the test. Legally produced is the other half — and it is the half Brazilian files usually skip.

S18.alt: "Livre de desmatamento" é metade do teste EUDR. "Produzido conforme a legislação brasileira" é a outra metade — direito de uso da terra, ambiental, trabalhista, tributário, anticorrupção, entre outros.

A19.alt: The due diligence statement is one form. The file behind it is the product.

S19.alt: Your buyer's due diligence statement is one form. The file behind it — kept for five years, open to inspection — carries your data.

A20.alt: "We are small, so 30 June 2027 applies to us." Probably not the date that matters.

S20.alt: "Somos pequenos, então o prazo é junho de 2027."

A21.alt: The structure of an EUDR supplier file that a buyer can use. Six folders. No software required.

S21.alt: Six folders. That is the EUDR supplier file structure from this morning's note.

A22.alt: After the Omnibus, the CSDDD applies to EU companies with more than 5,000 employees and over EUR 1.5 billion net worldwide turnover, from 26 July 2029. Fewer companies, later date.

S22.alt: A CSDDD ficou menor e mais tarde: mais de 5.000 funcionários, EUR 1,5 bilhão, aplicação em julho de 2029.

A23.alt: The contract moved before the law did. Read your supply agreement; the CSDDD is already in it.

S23.alt: "Supplier shall provide evidence of compliance upon request." Signed. Filed. Never tested against the file.

A24.alt: The Omnibus introduced a value-chain cap. Suppliers should understand it — and not over-read it.

S24.alt: O teto da cadeia de valor na CSRD limita o que o comprador europeu pode pedir ao fornecedor com menos de 1.000 funcionários: no máximo, o conteúdo do padrão voluntário para PMEs (VSME).

A25.alt: Anatomy of one clause. "Supplier shall provide evidence of compliance with applicable environmental and social requirements upon Buyer's reasonable request."

S25.alt: Fourteen words. Five undefined terms. One termination clause two pages later.

A26.alt: The EU-wide civil liability regime was removed from the CSDDD. Buyers reacted by tightening contracts, not loosening them.

S26.alt: O comprador europeu dá uma nota de risco ao seu fornecedor. Ele não vai te contar a nota. Você vai ver no volume do próximo ano.

A27.alt: What a Brazilian board should see about EU supplier evidence. One page. Four blocks.

S27.alt: Exposure. Status. Gap. Decision. The one-page board file from this morning's note.

A28.alt: The one-page supplier evidence index. If you build only one document this quarter, build this.

S28.alt: Um índice de evidências de uma página: obrigação, fonte, comprador, documento, status, responsável, próxima data.

A29.alt: Your emissions are your buyer's Scope 3. That sentence explains most of the data requests you receive that are not labelled CBAM.

S29.alt: Your buyer is estimating your emissions with an industry average. You can replace that estimate with your number — documented, allocated, periodised.

A30.alt: Thirty notes. One thesis: European buyers decide on evidence, and most Brazilian evidence is not yet usable by anyone outside the company that holds it.

S30.alt: A revisão termina. O comprador continua pedindo.
